documents.title: Amazing Grace
documents.text:
Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound!)
That saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found,—
Was blind, but now I see.

documents.title: Amazing Grace
documents.text:
'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
And grace my fears relieved;
How precious did that grace appear
The hour I first believed!

documents.title: Amazing Grace
documents.text:
Through many dangers, toils, and snares.
I have already come;
'Tis grace has brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.

documents.title: Danny Boy
documents.text:
Oh, Danny Boy, the pipes, the pipes are calling
From glen to glen, and down the mountain side,
The summer's gone, and all the roses falling,
It's you, it's you must go and I must bide.
But come ye back when summer's in the meadow,
Or when the valley's hushed and white with snow,
It's I'll be here in sunshine or in shadow,
Oh, Danny Boy, oh Danny Boy, I love you so!

documents.title: Danny Boy
documents.text:
But when ye come, and all the flowers are dying,
If I am dead, as dead I well may be,
Ye'll come and find the place where I am lying,
And kneel and say an Ave there for me;
And I shall hear, though soft you tread above me,
And all my grave will warmer, sweeter be,
For you will bend and tell me that you love me,
And I shall sleep in peace until you come to me!

documents.title: Go Down, Moses
documents.text:
When Israel was in Egypt's land
Let my people go
Oppress'd so hard they could not stand
Let my people go

documents.title: Go Down, Moses
documents.text:
Go down, Moses
Way down in Egypt's land
Tell old Pharaoh
Let my people go

documents.title: Take Me Out to the Ball Game
documents.text:
Katie Casey was baseball mad,
Had the fever and had it bad.
Just to root for the home town crew,
Ev'ry sou
Katie blew.
On a Saturday her young beau
Called to see if she'd like to go
To see a show, but Miss Kate said "No,
I'll tell you what you can do:"

documents.title: Take Me Out to the Ball Game
documents.text:
Take me out to the ball game,
Take me out with the crowd;
Buy me some peanuts and Cracker Jack,
I don't care if I never get back.
Let me root, root, root for the home team
If they don't win, it's a shame.
For it's one, two, three strikes, you're out,
At the old ball game.

documents.title: Take Me Out to the Ball Game
documents.text:
Katie Casey saw all the games,
Knew the players by their first names.
Told the umpire he was wrong,
All along,
Good and strong.
When the score was just two to two,
Katie Casey knew what to do,
Just to cheer up the boys she knew,
She made the gang sing this song:

documents.title: Yes! We Have No Bananas
documents.text:
There's a fruit store on our street, It's run by a Greek
And he keeps good things to eat, But you should hear him speak
When you ask him anything, he never answers no
He just "yesses" you to death, And as he takes your dough he tells you

documents.title: Yes! We Have No Bananas
documents.text:
Yes! We have no bananas, We have no bananas today
We've string beans and HON-ions, cab-BAH-ges and scallions; And all kinds of fruit and say
We have an old fashioned to-MAH-to, Long Island po-TAH-to
But yes! We have no bananas, We have no bananas today

documents.title: Yes! We Have No Bananas

Bus'ness got so good with him; He wrote home to say
"Send me Pete and Nick and Jim, I need help right away"
When he got them in the store, there was fun you bet
Someone asked for "Sparrowgrass", And the whole quartette all answered

documents.title: Changes
documents.text: This posthumously released song discusses societal conflicts, addressing issues related to Tupac's era of influence such as race relations, classism, police brutality, drugs, and gang violence. It contrasts the difficulties of life in the ghetto with broader global conflicts, mentions Black Panther Party founder Huey P. Newton, and imagines the possibility of a Black U.S. president alongside the singer picturing his own death. The track became a number-one hit in Norway and the Netherlands and was performed by American rapper 2Pac with the R&B trio Talent.

documents.title: Fast Car
documents.text: This folk-pop song tells the story of a working woman and a couple trying to escape the cycle of poverty and make a life together while facing challenges. It is not directly autobiographical, but rather represents the struggles of working-class people in a community observed by the writer growing up. The debut single was written and performed by American singer-songwriter Tracy Chapman.

documents.title: Jolene
documents.text: Written from the perspective of a narrator who worries a stunningly beautiful woman with red hair and green eyes will take her husband, the song is a direct plea begging that woman not to steal away her partner. Based on a true story about a bank clerk who once flirted with the singer's husband, it addresses the rival directly to implore her not to take him just because she can. It was written and recorded by the American country singer Dolly Parton.

documents.title: What Was I Made For?
documents.text: "What Was I Made For?" was written by Billie Eilish and Finneas O'Connell for the soundtrack to the fantasy comedy film Barbie. Inspired by the film, its character, and the way the character would feel, the song also parallels the plot of Barbie and accompanies a scene where Barbie meets the spirit of her creator, Ruth Handler. The song was released as a single by American singer-songwriter Billie Eilish.

documents.title: Jingle Bells (the Batman playground parody)
documents.text: This well-known playground parody of Jingle Bells has a catchy, simple melody and mocks Batman and Robin with various playful variations. It has been frequently referenced and sung across different television media, including animated series and holiday specials.
